title: Parameter-Controlled Regime Transitions in Energy-Flow Cosmology: Cross-Sector Consistency Between Lensing and Background Observables
description: Reports controlled scans of the sealed EFC lensing engine showing that the kinetic stiffness K0 dominantly sets the redshift of the predicted sign-changing Σeff(z) crossover, while amplitude parameters have minor impact. Documents cross-sector consistency (µ < 1) between sealed lensing and growth sectors, establishes robustness to power-spectrum choice, and pre-registers joint falsification tests for Euclid DR1 and DESI DR2.

P1_crossover.description: Pre-registered EFC prediction for the redshift where the effective weak-lensing coupling \Sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}(z) changes sign (non-monotonic lensing slip).

P2_growth.description: Sealed EFC prediction for the linear growth observable at z = 0.7.

horndeski_constraint.description: Empirical property reported for Horndeski models (Peirone et al. 2018) used here as a contrast: surveyed non-EFC frameworks predict monotonic profiles without a sign-changing \Sigma_{\mathrm{eff}}.

mu_sign.description: Both EFC sectors (lensing and growth) predict entropic damping of the Newtonian potential (\mu < 1), providing qualitative cross-sector consistency.

K0_control.description: Scan results from the sealed lensing engine: K0 dominantly controls the crossover redshift, while large rescalings of amplitude parameters have comparatively minor effect.

key_results.main_finding: The sealed EFC lensing engine robustly predicts a sign-changing, non-monotonic Σeff(z) with crossover near z ≈ 0.44, dominantly controlled by K0 (Δz ≈ 0.87 for K0 ∈ [0.5,4.0]) and only weakly by amplitude parameters (Δz ≈ 0.11 for ×50 rescaling), with the sign-change robust to power-spectrum choice (BBKS cross-check shifts ≤ 0.06) and consistent µ < 1 across lensing and growth sectors.
datasets_used: Symbiose Framework Atlas snapshot (2026-04-21) for comparative landscape

sealed_predictions.statement: Non-monotonic, sign-changing Σeff(z) with crossover at z = 0.44 ± 0.03.
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: Euclid DR1 tomographic cosmic shear and lensing cross-correlations measuring Σeff(z) over 0 < z < 1.
DESI DR2 redshift-space distortion measurements and joint growth analyses around z ≈ 0.7.

sealed_predictions.statement: EG statistic EG = 1.086 (pre-registered; pending kSZ-reconstructed estimators).
sealed_predictions.falsifiable_by: EG measurements combining lensing-galaxy and RSD with kSZ velocity reconstruction.

kill_criteria: KC1: Euclid DR1 finds Σeff(z) to be strictly monotonic with no sign change over 0 < z < 1 at ≥95% confidence, or measures a crossover redshift inconsistent with z = 0.44 ± 0.03 such that no EFC configuration (within K0 ∈ [0.5, 4.0] and ±×50 amplitude rescalings) can reproduce it.
KC2: DESI DR2 measures fσ8 at z = 0.7 outside the sealed window 0.430 ± 0.02 at ≥2σ (accounting for systematic error budgets), with no consistent EFC parameter realization.

KC3: Robust observational inference of µ ≥ 1 in the late-time universe (0.3 < z < 0.9) from growth and/or combined lensing+RSD, or a demonstrable µ-sign disagreement between the sealed lensing and growth sectors after consistent phenomenology-to-action mapping.

KC4: Joint Euclid+DESI constraints locate the Σeff crossover (if present) and µ–Σ quadrant in a region incompatible with EFC’s non-monotonic slip and µ < 1 (i.e., consistent with Horndeski monotonic behavior and (Σ−1)(µ−1) ≥ 0 without a sign change), excluding EFC across scanned parameter ranges.

KC5: Future EG measurements with kSZ reconstruction yield EG inconsistent with the pre-registered value 1.086 within forecasted uncertainties, in a way that cannot be reconciled within the EFC parameter space.
